subject.title: fix: setup fails closed for invalid configuration arguments

question: Should repeated value options remain backward-compatible first-value-wins, or should SetupEngine intentionally adopt strict duplicate-value rejection for all existing automation scripts?
rationale: Both outcomes are technically implementable, but choosing a permanent CLI compatibility contract affects existing unattended setup callers and cannot be settled from tests alone.

options.title: Preserve first-value-wins
options.body: Retain the established script contract while applying fail-closed validation to unknown, malformed, positional, and missing-value inputs.

options.title: Adopt strict duplicate rejection
options.body: Keep the PR's safer ambiguity rule, with explicit setup-owner approval and prominent upgrade documentation for affected scripts.

recommendation.title: Preserve first-value-wins
recommendation.body: Retain the established script contract while applying fail-closed validation to unknown, malformed, positional, and missing-value inputs.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior review explicitly framed the duplicate-value behavior as a setup-owner compatibility decision.
